hSampleText:
SAMPLE FREELANCE SERVICES AGREEMENT

Parties: the CLIENT and the FREELANCER.
1. Services: The Freelancer will design and build the Client’s website as the Client describes from time to time.
2. Fee: The total fee is 3,000 EUR, payable 90 days after final delivery. Late payment carries no interest.
3. Revisions: The Freelancer will make unlimited revisions at no extra charge until the Client is fully satisfied, in the Client’s sole judgment.
4. Intellectual property: All work, including the Freelancer’s pre-existing materials, belongs to the Client from the first day, whether or not the fee has been paid.
5. Termination: The Client may terminate at any time without notice and without paying for work done. The Freelancer may terminate only with 90 days’ written notice.
6. Liability: The Freelancer is liable without limit for all direct and indirect losses of the Client.
7. Renewal: This agreement renews automatically for 12 months unless the Freelancer cancels in writing at least 6 months before the end.
8. Disputes: Only the courts where the Client lives have jurisdiction, and the Freelancer pays all legal costs.

guideFlowAnalyzeIntro: To revise in your favor: bring the text in, lock your party, run analysis, read the decision card / radar / red flags, tap Apply shield to stitch clauses, then copy the ready message. Continue with Compare or export if needed.
guideFlowDiffIntro: DiffTool lives under the Analyze tab (not a separate tab). Compare original vs counterparty/your revised text in split or redline view. After a shield or a new counterparty draft, use Verify new version and paste into the empty box.
guideFlowExportIntro: Three outputs: (1) Analysis PDF report — score and summary. (2) Redline PDF — deletions/insertions highlighted. (3) Word (.docx) — clean stitched text after Apply shield. Apply first, then pick the right button.
guideFlowAdvisorIntro: This Guide only teaches how to use NexuLex; it does not interpret statutes or damages. For legal questions open Advisor, set party/country context, and type your question. Do not confuse Guide with Advisor.
guideFlowSettingsIntro: Under Settings you manage language, dark/light theme, password, and seat codes. Change the app language here independently of analysis language.
guideFlowPlaybookIntro: After analysis, the pre-signature playbook lists missing protections. With Pro you can send a read-only brief to advisor or household seats — the original contract never leaves.
guideStepAnalyzePaste: On the Analyze tab, paste the full contract into the large text box. Line breaks are kept — do not trim. This is step one of revise-in-your-favor.
guideStepAnalyzeUpload: No text? Use Pick PDF / document. The app extracts text; if it looks broken, re-pick or paste instead.
guideStepAnalyzeImages: For photo pages use Upload multiple contract images. Clear, upright pages extract better.
guideStepAnalyzeParty: Under “Who should we protect you as?” tap a dual card (named when radar finds Apex/Anadolu). Analyze, shield, and message follow that side; Other roles… opens the full list. Analyze stays blocked until you confirm.
guideStepAnalyzeStart: Tap Start AI Analysis. Watch the progress steps; when done you get the score, Mini-Radar, red flags, and decision card.
guideStepAnalyzeDecision: Read the Security Score, Mini-Radar (parties/law/notice), and red flags. The decision card suggests SIGN / NEGOTIATE / WALK_AWAY — high risk can still be NEGOTIATE when remediable.
guideStepAnalyzeShield: Tap Apply shield to stitch selected counter-clauses into the text — that is revise-in-your-favor made concrete. After Apply you can share Word or redline PDF.
guideStepAnalyzeReady: On the decision card tap Copy message for the ready-to-send text, then paste into WhatsApp/email. Or use Share this card for a short social summary.
guideStepDiffOpen: On Analyze, open Compare in the workspace toggle. Diff is not a main tab by itself.
guideStepDiffOriginal: Original sits on one side (often your last analysis text); revised/counterparty on the other. Paste the new version into the empty box — do not wipe the original.
guideStepDiffSplit: Use Compare with counterparty text (split) to read both drafts side by side and scan what changed.
guideStepDiffRedline: Redline strikes deletions and highlights insertions. On long texts wait for the spinner; if scroll feels stuck, swipe the list — not the dimmed backdrop.
guideStepDiffAfter: After a shield or a new counterparty draft, use Verify new version: original is prefilled; paste the new text in the empty box and review the diff.
guideStepExportApply: First tap Apply shield so selected counters stitch into the body. Check which clauses are selected before you apply.
guideStepExportPdf: Download / share PDF report is the analytical report (score, summary, clauses). It is not the redline Diff export.
guideStepExportShare: Redline PDF is the visual redline with deletions/insertions. Share from the sheet; print preview should stay A4-legible.
guideStepExportDocx: Word (.docx) is the clean stitched text after Apply shield — not Word track-changes. Pick .docx from the post-Apply share row.
guideStepAdvisorVs: The Guide (this sheet) explains app usage. Advisor is legal Q&A. For statutes, damages, courts the Guide invents nothing — switch to Advisor.
guideStepAdvisorOpen: Switch to the Advisor tab in the top bar. Your analysis may provide context — still write a clear question.
guideStepAdvisorAsk: In Advisor confirm party/country context, then send the question. Answers include humility/sources and do not replace Guide how-to steps.
guideStepAdvisorWhen: How-to (“how do I download PDF?”) → Guide. Legal (“is this clause void?”) → Ask legal advisor.
guideStepSettingsOpen: Open the Settings tab from the top bar. Language, theme, security, and seat codes live here.
guideStepSettingsLang: Pick one of 13 languages under App language. Report language can differ — do not confuse them.
guideStepPlaybookOpen: Scroll the analysis result and open Pre-signature playbook. Tick missing protections — the shield feeds on them.
guideStepPlaybookSeat: In Settings use Advisor seat / Household seat to mint a read-only brief code. The original contract is not sent; respect Pro limits.

scenarioAskAdvisorPrompt: Please help me clarify my situation based on this scenario roadmap. Give general information only; do not invent precedents or win rates:
scenarioConsumerDesc: Defect → complaint → consumer mediation / arbitration hints.
scenarioConsumerEscalate_s1_detail: Photos/video, invoice, and a short defect description with dates.
scenarioConsumerEscalate_s2_detail: Send a written remedy request (repair/replace/refund) with a deadline.
scenarioConsumerEscalate_s3_detail: If ignored, prepare consumer mediation/arbitration filing materials for your country — verify local thresholds.
scenarioConsumerLawyer: Consult a consumer attorney if health/safety risk, high value, or the seller ignores formal complaints.
scenarioConsumerNegotiate_s1_detail: Save the partial offer and your purchase proof.
scenarioConsumerNegotiate_s2_detail: Propose a clear acceptable remedy without insults or invented legal threats.
scenarioConsumerNegotiate_s3_detail: If talks stall, move to formal consumer complaint channels with your file.
scenarioInvoiceDemand_s1_detail: Include invoice numbers, due dates, and bank details. Keep proof of send.
scenarioInvoiceDemand_s2_detail: One clear written follow-up with a final deadline.
scenarioInvoiceDemand_s3_detail: If unpaid, discuss notarized notice / mediation with counsel.
scenarioInvoiceDesc: Commercial debt → notice → optional mediation → court gate.
scenarioInvoiceDisputed_s1_detail: Keep invoices, delivery proofs, and dispute emails together.
scenarioInvoiceDisputed_s2_detail: List agreed vs disputed amounts in writing without admitting liability you disagree with.
scenarioInvoiceDisputed_s3_detail: Consider commercial mediation with counsel if talks fail.
scenarioInvoiceLarge_s1_detail: Contracts, POs, delivery notes, and invoice trail must align.
scenarioInvoiceLarge_s2_detail: Prefer attorney-drafted formal notice for large claims.
scenarioInvoiceLarge_s3_detail: Review mediation prerequisites and limitation periods with counsel before filing.
scenarioInvoiceLawyer: Use commercial counsel before notarized notices, mediation filings, or lawsuits — especially for large or disputed claims.
scenarioInvoiceStd_s1_detail: Ensure the buyer received goods/services and the invoice is correct.
scenarioInvoiceStd_s2_detail: Send a final demand with a short payment window.
scenarioInvoiceStd_s3_detail: If still unpaid, escalate to notarized notice or mediation with counsel.
scenarioLaborDefault_s1_detail: Gather contract, payroll, and exit letters before deciding next steps.
scenarioLaborDefault_s2_detail: Write a short list of what you believe is unpaid and why (dates, amounts).
scenarioLaborDefault_s3_detail: Use the advisor chat for a general Q&A, then consult an attorney for filing decisions.
scenarioLaborDesc: Unpaid severance, overtime, or unfair-dismissal framing.
scenarioLaborLawyerDefault: Consult a licensed labor attorney before filing any lawsuit or mediation application.
scenarioLaborLawyerPaid: Consult an attorney if you suspect underpayment despite a receipt, or if you signed a broad release under pressure.
scenarioLaborLawyerUnpaid: See a labor attorney if the employer refuses a written settlement, deadlines are near, or the claim is complex (multiple years / overtime stacks).
scenarioLaborPaidReview_s1_detail: Compare receipt totals to expected severance/notice using your tenure and last wage records.
scenarioLaborPaidReview_s2_detail: If you signed a release, note date and pressure context. Do not assume it is always invalid.
scenarioLaborPaidReview_s3_detail: If numbers look short or the release is sweeping, get a licensed review before further claims.
scenarioLaborUnpaidClaim_s1_detail: Separate severance, notice pay, overtime, and unused leave with rough date ranges.
scenarioLaborUnpaidClaim_s2_detail: Send a calm written follow-up citing the unpaid list. Avoid threats or invented statutes.
scenarioLaborUnpaidClaim_s3_detail: If unpaid after your deadline, discuss mediation/court gates with counsel — do not self-file complex claims alone.
scenarioLaborUnpaidNoNotice_s1_detail: Save contracts, payslips, timesheets, and termination messages. Do not delete chats.
scenarioLaborUnpaidNoNotice_s2_detail: Ask in writing for unpaid severance/notice items with a clear deadline. Keep proof of delivery.
scenarioLaborUnpaidNoNotice_s3_detail: Where required by local labor rules, prepare mediation or labor authority filing with your document pack.
scenarioLegalDisclaimer: This roadmap is general information only — not legal advice or court representation. No win-rate or precedent is invented. Consult a licensed attorney for your situation.
scenarioNdaDesc: Evidence preservation and notice framing — not a conviction.
scenarioNdaLawyer: Engage counsel before accusing anyone publicly or sending aggressive notices that could backfire.
scenarioNdaNotice_s1_detail: Label exhibits (dates, sources) without editing originals.
scenarioNdaNotice_s2_detail: Write a factual chronology for counsel — no invented damages figures.
scenarioNdaNotice_s3_detail: Prefer counsel-sent notices to reduce escalation and defamation risk.
scenarioNdaPreserve_s1_detail: Collect what you have without illegal access to systems.
scenarioNdaPreserve_s2_detail: Confirm you are still bound and what remedies the contract mentions.
scenarioNdaPreserve_s3_detail: Ask the advisor general questions, then consult counsel before formal notices.
scenarioNdaUrgent_s1_detail: Secure copies of suspected leaks. Avoid public accusations.
scenarioNdaUrgent_s2_detail: Note confidentiality scope, duration, and notice requirements from the signed NDA.
scenarioNdaUrgent_s3_detail: Have an attorney draft any cease-and-desist / evidence preservation letter.
scenarioRentDesc: Landlord or tenant unpaid rent and notice flow.
scenarioRentLandClaim_s1_detail: Check due date, deposit, and notice clauses in the signed lease.
scenarioRentLandClaim_s2_detail: Send a clear payment reminder with amount and account details.
scenarioRentLandClaim_s3_detail: If still unpaid after the deadline, prepare a formal notice pack with counsel guidance.
scenarioRentLandSevere_s1_detail: Build a month-by-month rent ledger with bank proofs. Avoid oral-only claims.
scenarioRentLandSevere_s2_detail: Send a dated written notice of arrears with a cure deadline. Keep delivery proof.
scenarioRentLandSevere_s3_detail: Discuss lawful eviction/enforcement options with counsel — never self-help lockouts.
scenarioRentLawyerLand: See a real-estate/lease attorney before eviction filings or lockouts — especially if notices are disputed.
scenarioRentLawyerTenant: See counsel urgently if you received an eviction notice, utility cutoff threat, or illegal lockout.
scenarioRentTenantNoticed_s1_detail: Note deadlines, claimed months, and how the notice was delivered.
scenarioRentTenantNoticed_s2_detail: If you dispute amounts or already paid, reply with proofs. Stay factual.
scenarioRentTenantNoticed_s3_detail: If eviction proceedings are threatened, contact a tenant/lease attorney promptly.
scenarioRentTenantProtect_s1_detail: Export bank proofs for every rent payment and keep the lease handy.
scenarioRentTenantProtect_s2_detail: If you will be late, propose a written catch-up plan before notices escalate.
scenarioRentTenantProtect_s3_detail: Ask the advisor for general info on local aids; verify with official sources or counsel.

pgStage_safety_d: If you or a child are in danger, call the emergency number now. Go to a safe place if you can; helplines and shelters help without a lawyer.
pgStage_evidence_d: Save messages, photos, receipts and documents, and note dates, places and witnesses while you remember them. Keep a copy outside your phone.
pgStage_deadline_d: Legal steps often have strict time limits, some very short. Confirm the limit that applies to you and put it in your calendar with a margin.
pgStage_official_letter_d: If a court, enforcement office or authority wrote to you, check the response period stated in it. Missing it can make a decision final against you.
pgStage_written_demand_d: Send the other side a clear written request stating what you want and by when. Use a method that proves delivery and keep a copy.
pgStage_negotiate_d: A written settlement is often faster and cheaper than court. Do not sign anything you do not fully understand, and keep every agreement in writing.
pgStage_mediation_d: Mediation, arbitration boards or ombudsman schemes can solve the dispute without court. In some countries this step is required before you can sue.
pgStage_authority_d: Regulators and public bodies accept complaints, often online and free of charge. Keep the reference number and every reply.
pgStage_police_t: Report it to the police or prosecutor
pgStage_police_d: Report as soon as possible and ask for a written record or reference number. Bring your evidence and a short timeline.
pgStage_medical_d: See a doctor promptly and ask for a written report and copies of all records, tests and invoices. Medical records are key evidence.
pgStage_insurance_d: Inform the insurers involved quickly and in writing; policies often require prompt notice. Do not accept a settlement before you understand your claim.
pgStage_legal_aid_d: If your income is limited you may qualify for free or low-cost legal aid. Bar associations and legal aid offices can tell you how to apply.
pgStage_court_d: If nothing else works, file a claim with the competent court. Many countries offer simplified or online procedures for smaller amounts.
pgStage_hearing_d: Bring a one-page timeline, copies of every document and your witnesses’ details. Keep to facts and dates, and answer only what is asked.
pgStage_enforce_d: A judgment may need a separate enforcement step before you are paid. If you lose, appeal periods are usually short, so check yours at once.
pgStage_appeal_admin_d: Ask the authority for its decision and reasons in writing, then file an objection or appeal within the period stated in the decision.
pgStage_rights_d: In most countries you may remain silent, ask for a lawyer and an interpreter, and ask why you are held. Stay calm and do not sign what you do not understand.
pgStage_contact_d: Inform a family member, a lawyer or, if you are a foreign national, your consulate. Write down names, places and times.
pgStage_children_d: Courts focus on the child’s best interests. Keep routines stable, keep children out of the conflict and document your care role.
pgStage_inventory_d: Make a list of property, accounts, debts and key documents with values and dates. It is the basis of any division or claim.
pgStage_inheritance_decision_t: Decide whether to accept the estate
pgStage_inheritance_decision_d: In many countries heirs can also inherit debts, and there may be a time limit to accept or refuse. Check the debts before you decide.
pgStage_takedown_d: Use the platform’s report or legal request form. Save the link, date and screenshots first, in case the content disappears.
pgStage_data_request_d: Ask the company in writing for access to, correction or deletion of your personal data. If it does not answer properly, complain to the data protection authority.
pgStage_status_d: Apply or renew before your permit expires and keep the proof of application. Check whether you may work or travel while your application is pending.
pgStage_keep_paying_d: Unless a lawyer advises otherwise, keep paying undisputed rent, tax or instalments so the other side cannot use it against you.
pgStage_secure_accounts_d: Call your bank at once to block cards or transfers, change passwords and turn on two-step login. Never send more money to recover a loss.
pg_divorce_desc: Ending a marriage: agreement or court, children, home, property and support.
pg_divorce_focus: An agreed divorce is usually faster, cheaper and calmer. Put every agreement on children, home, money and debts in writing before you sign.
pg_divorce_lawyer: Always when there are children, significant property, violence or a spouse abroad.
pg_child_support_desc: Getting or changing maintenance for a child.
pg_child_support_focus: Support is usually based on the child’s needs and both parents’ income. Keep proof of every payment made or missed.
pg_child_support_lawyer: When the other parent hides income, lives abroad or stops paying after a decision.
pg_inheritance_desc: A relative died: estate, heirs, will, debts and sharing.
pg_inheritance_focus: Find out about debts before accepting anything: in many systems you can refuse an estate, but often only within a limited time.
pg_inheritance_lawyer: When heirs disagree, a will is contested, or there is a business or property abroad.
pg_domestic_violence_desc: Violence, threats or control at home: safety, protection orders and support.
pg_domestic_violence_focus: Your safety comes first. Protection orders can often be obtained quickly, and helplines support you confidentially.
pg_domestic_violence_lawyer: As soon as you are safe: a lawyer or legal aid office can apply for protection and handle custody and housing.
pg_dismissal_desc: You were fired or pushed to resign: pay, compensation and challenging it.
pg_dismissal_focus: Deadlines to challenge a dismissal can be very short. Do not sign a resignation or settlement before you know your rights.
pg_dismissal_lawyer: Straight away if you want to challenge it, or you were dismissed while ill, pregnant or after a complaint.
pg_unpaid_wages_desc: Salary, overtime or final pay not paid.
pg_unpaid_wages_focus: Payslips and bank statements are the core evidence. Claim in writing and keep your own record of hours worked.
pg_unpaid_wages_lawyer: When the amount is large, the employer is insolvent or you were not officially registered.
pg_workplace_harassment_desc: Bullying, sexual harassment or unequal treatment by colleagues or managers.
pg_workplace_harassment_focus: Write down every incident with date, words and witnesses. Use internal complaint channels in writing so there is a record.
pg_workplace_harassment_lawyer: When you face retaliation, your health suffers or you are thinking of leaving the job.
pg_tenant_rights_desc: Deposit not returned, repairs ignored, rent increases or eviction threats.
pg_tenant_rights_focus: A landlord usually needs a legal procedure to evict you. Do not leave or stop paying because of a threat alone.
pg_tenant_rights_lawyer: When you receive an official eviction notice or court papers.
pg_landlord_arrears_desc: As a landlord: arrears, damage and getting the property back.
pg_landlord_arrears_focus: Never change the locks or remove belongings yourself: self-help eviction is illegal in most countries. Use the legal procedure.
pg_landlord_arrears_lawyer: Before you start an eviction, or when the tenant disputes the debt.
pg_neighbor_dispute_desc: Noise, damage, boundaries, trees, leaks and shared property.
pg_neighbor_dispute_focus: Keep a dated log of each incident. A calm talk or mediation solves most neighbour disputes better than court.
pg_neighbor_dispute_lawyer: When there is structural damage, a boundary conflict or threats.
pg_consumer_refund_desc: Refund, repair or replacement for a purchase that went wrong.
pg_consumer_refund_focus: Complain to the seller in writing first and keep the receipt. Consumer bodies and dispute boards are often free.
pg_consumer_refund_lawyer: Rarely needed; consider it for expensive goods, vehicles or when you were injured.
pg_scam_victim_desc: Money lost to fraud, a fake shop, phishing or an investment scam.
pg_scam_victim_focus: Speed matters: call your bank immediately. The sooner a transfer is reported, the better the chance to stop it.
pg_scam_victim_lawyer: When the loss is large or your identity was stolen. Beware of “recovery” offers: they are often a second scam.
pg_debt_defense_desc: Payment orders, collection letters or enforcement for a debt.
pg_debt_defense_focus: If you dispute the debt, object within the period on the official document. Silence often makes the claim enforceable.
pg_debt_defense_lawyer: When you receive court or enforcement papers, or the debt is not yours.
pg_small_claim_desc: Recovering a loan, deposit or unpaid amount from a person.
pg_small_claim_focus: A clear written demand with a final date solves many cases. Keep proof of the payment and of every promise to repay.
pg_small_claim_lawyer: When the amount is large or the debtor has assets abroad.
pg_business_invoice_desc: A client does not pay: reminders, late-payment interest and collection.
pg_business_invoice_focus: Check the contract for payment terms, interest and jurisdiction clauses before you escalate.
pg_business_invoice_lawyer: When the client disputes the work, is insolvent or is based in another country.
pg_traffic_accident_desc: Accident with injuries or damage: police, insurance and compensation.
pg_traffic_accident_focus: Secure the scene and get medical help first. Photos, witness details and a joint report are key; do not admit fault at the scene.
pg_traffic_accident_lawyer: When someone was injured, the insurer refuses or liability is disputed.
pg_medical_error_desc: Harm after treatment: records, complaints and compensation.
pg_medical_error_focus: Request your full medical file in writing. An independent medical opinion is usually the heart of the case.
pg_medical_error_lawyer: Early on: medical cases are complex and need expert evidence.
pg_crime_victim_desc: Theft, assault, threats or other crimes: report, support and compensation.
pg_crime_victim_focus: Report quickly and keep the reference number. Victims often have rights to information, support services and compensation.
pg_crime_victim_lawyer: When you want to take part in the proceedings or claim compensation.
pg_police_questioning_desc: Your rights if the police question, detain or accuse you.
pg_police_questioning_focus: You usually have the right to remain silent and to a lawyer. Ask for a lawyer before you answer questions.
pg_police_questioning_lawyer: Immediately: ask for a lawyer or a legal aid lawyer before any interview.
pg_online_defamation_desc: Insults, false statements or private images published online.
pg_online_defamation_focus: Preserve evidence before reporting, as content often disappears once flagged. Sharing intimate images without consent is a crime in many countries.
pg_online_defamation_lawyer: When the content harms your job or reputation, or the author is anonymous.
pg_data_privacy_desc: A company misuses your data, refuses deletion or had a data breach.
